facts.text: The San José de la Laguna Mission, built by Franciscan missionaries between 1699 and 1701, blends Pueblo-style adobe with Spanish religious architecture and still stands in Mesita.
Mesita’s church, dedicated to the Assumption of the Virgin Mary, Saint Anthony, and the Sacred Heart of Jesus, hosts August 15 celebrations blending Pueblo customs with Catholic traditions.
Along historic Route 66, Mesita became a stopover that fused indigenous heritage with mid‑20th‑century roadside culture, making it a unique roadside landmark.
Mesita emerged as one of six principal villages of the Laguna Pueblo, serving as a traditional farming and ceremonial hub within the network.
Archaeological surveys reveal Mesita’s occupation dates back to at least 6500 BCE, with a surge of diverse pottery styles appearing in the 13th‑14th centuries.
Perched on a defensive mesa top, Mesita lay along ancient trade routes, enabling seasonal habitations and floodwater farming by AD 1500.
